BILL NUMBER:  S1940

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to the tribal-state
compact revenue account; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon the expiration thereof


 PURPOSE :

Provides for a plan of expenditure for monies appropriated and
received by the state on behalf of a gaming facility located in the
City of Buffalo.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends subdivision 3 of section 99-h of the state finance
law, as amended by chapter 747 of the laws of 2006 to provide that
twenty five percent of the net drop from electronic gaming devices
from any gaming facility located in the City of Buffalo shall be
distributed in accordance with subdivision five of this section.

Section 2 amends subdivision 3 of section 99-h of the state finance
law, as amended by section 1 of part V of chapter 59 of the laws of
2006 to clarify that the municipal government entitled to receive the
minimum twenty five percent of the state share of the tribal-state
compact electronic gaming device revenues is to be the City of
Buffalo.

Section 3 amends section 99-h of the state finance law, as amended by
chapter 747 of the laws of 2006, by adding a new subdivision 5 by
specifying that the City of Buffalo will retain 96.5% of the total
annual amount received, and 3.5% will be allocated for the
development, preservation and expansion of cultural institutions or
the development and preservation of tourism resources.

 EXISTING LAW :

Current law does not specify the "host community" entitled to the
revenues provided for in the tribal-state compact.

 JUSTIFICATION :

According to the agreement between the Seneca Nation of the Indians
and the City of Buffalo, the city agreed to provide sewer, water and
emergency services to the proposed Buffalo Creek Casino. That
agreement acknowledged the intention of the Seneca Nation that the
city be designated as the sole host municipality, bolstering the fact
that the County of Erie was neither a party nor a signatory to the
agreement.

The county has also previously expressed its' opposition to such a
facility, repeatedly demonstrating such opposition to the construction
and operation of a casino on the Buffalo Creek Casino site by
participating in three separate lawsuits. The county's efforts in this
regard have led city government to spend approximately $400,000 to
fight these lawsuits, a fact which should preclude county government
from any effort to obtain revenues as a "host community" under
existing statute.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill- 2008. Referred to Finance.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to New York State.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Positive for the City of Buffalo

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Provides for a plan of expenditure for monies appropriated and received by the state on behalf of a gaming facility located in the city of Buffalo; provides for the repeal of such provisions on December 31, 2018.
